drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 51-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.82, creatinine 0.68-0.7, hemoglobin 14.3-14.5, platelets 202-207, sodium 124-126, wbc 7.6-8; vitals dbp 70-74, heart_rate 84-88, map 90-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-17, sbp 127-133, spo2 96-98, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Fluid restriction 1.2 L/day; Sodium chloride 1 g PO TID
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.68-0.73, hemoglobin 14.3-14.4, platelets 197-207, sodium 127-129, wbc 7.3-8; vitals dbp 69-73, heart_rate 85-88, map 89-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 128-135, spo2 96-98, temp 36.9-37.2
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 51-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
